title: Introduce lint-orchestrator composite action and incremental test selector for fast CI feedback
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a composite GitHub Action (lint-orchestrator) that unifies linting across TS/Python/Go and an incremental test selector for quicker CI runs. Improves dev feedback loop and reduces CI cost. Includes docs for local dev usage and a small follow-up to expand test ownership map.
description:
Motivation: CI runtime and noise from multiple lint runners has increased feedback time. We want a single orchestrated action that runs language-specific linters in a predictable order, supports incremental linting based on changed files, and exposes a local fastpath. Additionally, large test suites are expensive; this PR adds an incremental test selector which picks affected tests using git diff + a small test-ownership map to run a smaller subset on pull requests (with a full test gate on release branches).

What this PR does:
- Adds .github/actions/lint-orchestrator: a composite action that sequences ruff/flake8 (Python), eslint/tsc (TypeScript), golangci-lint (Go), and pre-commit hooks. The action supports an INPUT_CHANGED_ONLY flag to limit linters to modified files.
- Introduces tools/test-selector/select-tests.py: a lightweight selector that maps changed files to test suites (pytest, jest, go test). It uses simple YAML ownership rules and falls back to full-test when uncertain.
- Updates CI workflows to use lint-orchestrator and a new staged test lane (fastpath for incremental tests, full for release).
- Pins linter versions and bump automation: golangci-lint -> v1.59.0, ruff -> 0.20.0, eslint -> 8.44.0; adds a compatibility shim in .github/actions/lint-orchestrator to surface version mismatches.
- Adds README-ci.md documenting local fastpath and how to run the selector locally.

Checklist:
- [x] Design: ENG-2412 
- [x] Implement composite action and selector
- [x] Update CI workflows and add staged lanes
- [x] Docs for local developer flow
- [x] Manual verification on a small set of PRs

Testing & verification summary:
- Ran lint-orchestrator in sandbox -> initially failed due to ruff minor API change; pinned ruff to 0.20.0 and re-ran.
- Fastpath CI lane ran on this PR: test selector chose 12 of ~3500 tests (~0.3%); all passed.
- Full test lane (release-main) remains unchanged and gated.

Backward compatibility & rollout:
- Default behavior of workflows is unchanged (full lint + full tests) unless repo-level flag fastpath-enabled=true is set for the branch or PR. We staged rollout by enabling fastpath for contributor teams and monitoring flaky rate for 48h.

Follow-ups planned:
- Expand ownership map across more packages (ENG-2468).
- Add telemetry to measure selector precision/recall and CI time savings.

Changed files (high level):
- .github/actions/lint-orchestrator/action.yml
- .github/actions/lint-orchestrator/entrypoint.sh
- tools/test-selector/select-tests.py
- tools/test-selector/ownership.yaml
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (staged lanes: fastpath, full)
- README-ci.md
- pyproject.toml (ruff pinned)
- package.json (eslint bump)
- go.mod / .golangci.yml (golangci-lint bump)
- scripts/ci-runner.sh (small integration glue)

Notes on design choices:
- Composite action: chosen over separate workflows so we can gate and centralize linting policies and report aggregated status. This also simplifies local invocation (act or local runner).
- Selector: intentionally conservative. If selector is unsure, it signals full-test to avoid regressions. Ownership map editable by teams; we included a small default mapping for core packages.

Security considerations:
- Linter pins avoid surprise behavior from upstream. Composite action validates versions and fails fast if runner images are out-of-date.

Rollout record:
- 2026-02-16: enabled fastpath for infra and SDK teams
- 2026-02-18: observed 42% median CI time reduction for fastpath runs, 0.3% increase in flaky detection (investigating)
- 2026-02-20: merged and staged to main; follow-up ticket ENG-2468 created for ownership expansion

review_thread: Maya Chen: Nice consolidation. Can we ensure the composite action returns a single aggregated failure code so UI shows a single status?

Omar Patel: Selector looks promising. Two asks: (1) add a dry-run mode that prints selected tests without running, (2) please document how to update ownership.yaml.
Priya Shah: Added --dry-run and expanded README-ci.md with ownership editing instructions. Also added a validation step in CI to catch malformed ownership maps.
Lucas Fernandez: Observed that golangci-lint v1.59 flags an import alias change required in pkg/scheduler; please confirm fix is safe.
